newsitem.title: UK: Laura Ashley warns on current year profits.
newsitem.headline: Laura Ashley warns on current year profits.

text.p: British fashion and furniture retailer Laura Ashley Holdings Plc said on Thursday profits rose 57 percent last year to 16.2 million pounds, but warned earnings in the current year would be lower than expected.

The retailer said the need to mark-down prices on its current clothing range would affect first-half trading. "As a result the outcome for the full year, although ahead of last year, will be below current market expectations," the company said in a statement.
Group sales in the year to January 25 1997 rose to 327.6 million pounds ($532.1 million) from 336.6 million. The dividend was increased to 1.0 penny a share from 0.5.

The firm, founded in the 1950s by husband and wife team Bernard and Laura Ashley, is in the middle of a major drive to restructure and streamline operations after suffering from over-expansion and under-investment.
Chief executive Ann Iverson, who was brought in in 1995 to overhaul the business, said she was pleased with the substantial profit improvement.
"Although the current year will be difficult, we continue to remain a results driven group to ensure that we maxmise the potential of this powerful brand."

Sales were up eight percent overall in Britain, but fell nine percent in North America partly due to planned store closures and curtailment of mail order. Trading in continental Europe was difficult, particularly in France, Germany and Austria. Like-for-like sales on a common currency basis were down three percent in both clothing and home furnishings.
The group spent 13.8 million pounds last year on improved information systems and its shop expansion programme. This year it expects to spend about nine million pounds on expanding its stores.
